provenance.note: Generated by drivers/regression on the pystatsval harness against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==4.2.4. The 4.2.4 change is the Apple Silicon (MPS) float32 GLM IRLS inner solve: it moves from a Cholesky of XtWX to a gated matrix-free conjugate gradient on H v = Xt(W(X v)) (squaring-free; the host float64 Newton-decrement acceptance gate is unchanged). On the GPU GLM stability grid (Poisson/Gamma, n up to 500k, p up to 128) the convergence OUTCOMES are unchanged from 4.2.3 -- the plain (unpenalized) float32 log-link fit converges and ridge holds on both MPS and CUDA -- because the 4.2.3 Newton-decrement stop already cleared the premature-stop false negative; 4.2.4 changes HOW the MPS float32 inner solve is computed (gated CG, squaring-free) so it no longer relies on a positive-definite float32 Cholesky. CUDA and CPU paths are UNCHANGED and match 4.2.3 exactly. Correctness vs R is unchanged (round-off). MPS rows produced on torch 2.12.1 (version-sensitive solver envelope; the host float64 gate is the version-independent fail-loud guarantee). Hosts: powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2) and forge (NVIDIA CUDA, CPU fp64 + CUDA fp32/fp64, R 4.3.3).
provenance.baseline: Compare against reports/regression-v4.2.3.md. Correctness, CPU speed, and CUDA stability are unchanged (round-off / same outcomes). The only change is the MPS float32 GLM inner solve (Cholesky -> gated matrix-free CG, 4.2.4); on this stability grid the MPS plain/ridge convergence outcomes are identical to 4.2.3, but the float32 solve no longer forms or factorizes XtWX, removing the fp32 Cholesky-breakdown failure mode.

reference.name: R stats::lm / stats::glm / MASS::glm.nb
reference.what: R's lm() (OLS via pivoted QR) and glm() (GLM via IRLS), plus MASS::glm.nb() for the negative binomial. pystatistics unifies lm and glm, so the head-to-head pulls from both. Ridge is cross-checked against MASS::lm.ridge / glmnet in the drivers.

studies.title: Correctness vs R — Powerhouse (Apple Silicon, CPU / fp64)
studies.note: CPU OLS + 5 GLM families vs R on real datasets. Coefficients match R to round-off (~1e-11..1e-15; negbin coef ~1e-4 and gamma/poisson SEs ~1e-3..1e-8 are the documented dispersion/theta tolerances). As of 4.2.2 the CPU fit also MEETS/BEATS R on wall-clock (speedup_vs_r 1.4-2.8x here) -- the Prime-Directive parity requirement.

studies.title: Correctness vs R — Forge (Linux x86-64, CPU / fp64)
studies.note: Second-host CPU-vs-R correctness (Forge, R 4.3.3): identical round-off agreement; CPU speedup_vs_r 2.2-5x (CPU beats R).

studies.title: Device scaling — Powerhouse: CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32)
studies.note: OLS + GLM device scaling, CPU (fp64) vs MPS (fp32). As of 4.2.4 the MPS float32 GLM inner solve is a gated matrix-free conjugate gradient (squaring-free); convergence and timing on this grid match 4.2.3. The CPU baseline reflects the 4.2.2 Core-QR; the GPU is faster where float32 is stable.

studies.title: Device scaling — Forge: CPU (fp64) vs CUDA (fp32)
studies.note: OLS + GLM device scaling, CPU (fp64) vs CUDA (fp32).

studies.title: GPU GLM stability at scale — Powerhouse (MPS): plain converges, ridge holds
studies.note: GPU GLM stability at scale (MPS). The plain (unpenalized) float32 log-link fit converges and ridge holds -- unchanged from 4.2.3. 4.2.4 changes the MPS float32 inner solve to a gated matrix-free conjugate gradient (squaring-free; host float64 acceptance gate unchanged), so the float32 solve no longer relies on a positive-definite float32 Cholesky, but the convergence outcomes on this grid are identical. fp64 is unsupported on MPS (no float64).

studies.title: GPU GLM stability at scale — Forge (CUDA): plain, ridge, and fp64
studies.note: GPU GLM stability at scale (CUDA). Plain float32 log-link now CONVERGES (~1e-6 vs CPU, was fail-loud at 3.20.0); ridge converges; gpu_fp64 is exact (~1e-15). The 4.2.3 fp32 stop-rule fix resolved the plain-log-link failure on CUDA as well as MPS.

record_fields.coef_max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and R over the coefficient vector (correctness headline)
record_fields.se_max_rel: max relative difference over the standard-error vector
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.peak_mem_mb: peak memory during the fit (GPU allocator high-water mark; process RSS delta on CPU)
record_fields.plain_status: outcome of a plain GPU GLM fit at scale: converged or raised (fails loud when float32 is unreliable)
record_fields.ridge_status: outcome of a ridge GPU GLM fit (the penalty conditions the float32 solve)
record_fields.ridge_rel_vs_cpu_ridge: ||Δβ||/||β|| of the ridge GPU fit vs the CPU ridge fit (float32 tier)
record_fields.fp64_status: gpu_fp64 outcome — converged on CUDA, unsupported on MPS (no float64)
record_fields.fp64_rel_vs_cpu: ||Δβ||/||β|| of the gpu_fp64 fit vs the CPU fit (~1e-15, numerically exact)
